content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make wonton wrappers, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Rest the kneaded dough (30 minutes)
Step 2. Sift all-purpose flour into a large bowl (2 minutes)
Step 3. Measure out the cornstarch for dusting (1 minute)
Step 4. Divide the dough into four equal quarters (4 minutes)
Step 5. Stack the cut wrappers with cornstarch in between (5 minutes)
Step 6. Cut the rolled dough into 3-inch squares (8 minutes)
Step 7. Crack the eggs into a small ramekin (1 minute)
Step 8. Clean the kitchen counter surface (5 minutes)
Step 9. Wipe down the mixing area (10 minutes)
Step 10. Sanitize the rolling pin (2 minutes)
Step 11. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt (2 minutes)
Step 12. Calibrate the kitchen scale (1 minute)
Step 13. Measure the warm water (1 minute)
Step 14. Create a well in the center of the flour (1 minute)
Step 15. Whisk the eggs and water together (2 minutes)
Step 16. Prepare the storage containers (3 minutes)
Step 17. Organize the work station layout (5 minutes)
Step 18. Weigh the flour for accuracy (2 minutes)
Step 19. Retrieve the pasta machine from the pantry (3 minutes)
Step 20. Knead the dough until smooth (10 minutes)
Step 21. Squeeze out excess air from the dough (1 minute)
Step 22. Label the freezer bags (2 minutes)
Step 23. Check the consistency of the egg wash (30 seconds)
Step 24. Clean the whisk (2 minutes)
Step 25. Add the eggs to the flour well (1 minute)
Step 26. Dispose of the eggshells (1 minute)
Step 27. Combine the wet and dry ingredients (5 minutes)
Step 28. Set out the mixing bowl (1 minute)
Step 29. Sift the cornstarch to remove lumps (3 minutes)
Step 30. Gather all necessary ingredients (5 minutes)
Step 31. Wash your hands thoroughly (40 seconds)
Step 32. Lightly flour the work surface (1 minute)
Step 33. Dust the pasta machine rollers (2 minutes)
Step 34. Check the pantry for salt (2 minutes)
Step 35. Set the timer for the dough rest (30 seconds)
Step 36. Warm the water to 100 degrees (3 minutes)
Step 37. Clear a space on the table for rolling (5 minutes)
Step 38. Roll the dough through the thinnest setting (15 minutes)
Step 39. Sharpen the dough cutter (6 minutes)
Step 40. Lightly oil the pasta machine gears (4 minutes)
Step 41. Wrap the dough in plastic wrap (2 minutes)
Step 42. Put away the flour bag (2 minutes)
Step 43. Rinse the measuring cups (3 minutes)
Step 44. Inspect the dough for dry spots (1 minute)
Step 45. Place cornstarch in a shaker (2 minutes)
Step 46. Adjust the pasta machine thickness setting (30 seconds)
Step 47. Prepare a damp cloth to cover the dough (2 minutes)
Step 48. Check the sharpness of the square cutter (1 minute)
Step 49. Fetch the thermometer (1 minute)
Step 50. Pour the water into a measuring jug (30 seconds)
